summary: Required-checks SSOT: per-repo instance and a gate that runs

delivery.outcome: Each adopting repository owns a truthful .governance/required-checks.json validated against a pinned schema, and the gate that verifies it runs in the adopter under the same check names the ruleset enforces, instead of raising FileNotFoundError
nonGoals: No change to any repository's actual ruleset or enforced check names
No standard version bump in adopting repositories in this ticket
No change to validator-agent dispatch mechanics
No edit to the hub's own governance/required-checks.json

architecture.decision: required-checks.json carries per-repository data, so it must not be distributed with strategy=managed (pinned byte-identical). Reclassify it as extendable, the strategy already used for governance/manifest.default.json -> .governance/manifest.json, and add a managed required-checks.schema.json so the instance stays constrained. Resolve the gate's source relative to the script's own location, because package-manifest.json relocates it from scripts/ to .governance/ without adjusting its hardcoded path. Parse a job's name: field as the published check context, because that display name is what a GitHub ruleset requires; comparing against the job key only happens to work in the hub, where no job overrides its name. Widen the contract from a single workflowFile to a per-check binding, because ten adopting repositories draw their enforced contexts from two workflow files and cannot express that today; this must land with the strategy change or every instance would be migrated twice.
interfaceChanges: governance_check.py invokes the required-checks gate, so an adopter fails closed on a false declaration
dataChanges: Adopting repositories replace the inherited hub values with their own repository slug and the check names their ruleset enforces
architecture.rollback: Revert package-manifest.json strategy to managed and the two scripts; adopting repositories keep their existing locks untouched

validation.evidence: Hub gate still passes from its own location; regression guard for the path change
The existing test grows a case that copies the gate into a .governance/ layout; it fails on the current code and passes after the fix
The gate is invoked by governance_check.py, so it cannot stay orphaned again
The same test grows a case where a job overrides name:; the gate publishes that display name, so a declared value can match what the ruleset enforces
